annotations.description: Mulliganed a functional 7-card hand with 2 lands, Planar Atlas for mana fixing/ramp, and a solid curve of playable artifacts. While slightly land-light, Planar Atlas finds a third land and provides mana itself, making this hand quite keepable.
annotations.betterLine: Keep the 7-card hand. Play Island turn 1, Planar Atlas turn 2 (finding a land), Dutiful Replicator turn 3, Filigree Attendant turn 4. The hand has a clear game plan and Planar Atlas mitigates the land-light concern.

annotations.description: Played Universal Solvent (a nearly unactivatable artifact) instead of Locthwain Gargoyle, which provides an identical artifact count for Filigree Attendant but also offers a 0/3 blocker body immediately. Both will be deployed eventually, but getting the blocker down first is better when the opponent could develop threats.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Locthwain Gargoyle to get a 0/3 blocker on board immediately while still adding an artifact for Filigree Attendant. Deploy Universal Solvent next turn instead.

annotations.description: Passing in precombat main without using Aether Spellbomb to bounce Shambling Suit 4/3 (which is tapped from attacking). Bouncing it would allow Gearsmith Prodigy 2/2 and Phyrexian Broodlings 2/2 to attack into a much weaker board (just Locthwain Gargoyle 0/3 and summoning-sick Walking Ballista 1/1). The Spellbomb also powers Gearsmith Prodigy, so losing it reduces Prodigy to 1/2, but removing a 4/3 threat and enabling 4 damage of attacks could be worth it.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating any abilities
annotations.betterLine: Activate Aether Spellbomb paying {U} to bounce Shambling Suit back to opponent's hand before combat, then attack with both creatures for significant damage

annotations.description: Gem31P declined to attack with Gearsmith Prodigy and Phyrexian Broodlings when the opponent's only untapped blocker was Locthwain Gargoyle (0/3), which can't kill any attacker. At worst, one creature gets blocked and deals damage to the Gargoyle without dying, while the other deals 2 free damage. With the opponent having better late-game threats (Shambling Suit, Walking Ballista), applying pressure is important.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Gearsmith Prodigy and Phyrexian Broodlings to deal at least 2 guaranteed damage (likely 4 if opponent doesn't want to chump) with zero risk of losing a creature.

annotations.description: Casting Filigree Attendant pre-combat taps all 4 lands, losing the ability to hold Jace's Scrutiny as a combat trick. Casting Runed Servitor (2 mana) instead would also boost Shambling Suit to 5/3 (same artifact count increase) while leaving 2 mana open for Jace's Scrutiny during combat. Filigree Attendant has summoning sickness anyway so it can't attack this turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Filigree Attendant for {2}{U}{U} pre-combat, tapping out completely
annotations.betterLine: Cast Runed Servitor for {2} pre-combat (Suit still becomes 5/3), attack with Shambling Suit holding up Jace's Scrutiny as a combat trick, then evaluate post-combat options

annotations.description: Gem31P passed priority during combat damage step with Aether Spellbomb available and blue mana to activate it. They could have bounced the attacking Shambling Suit 5/3 back to the opponent's hand, which would both save their Gearsmith Prodigy 2/2 from dying in combat AND remove a major 5/3 threat that the opponent would need to recast. Instead, Gearsmith Prodigy will die and Shambling Suit survives.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, letting combat damage resolve normally — Gearsmith Prodigy dies, Shambling Suit survives.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Aether Spellbomb targeting Shambling Suit (paying {U} from the untapped Island) to bounce it back to opponent's hand, saving Gearsmith Prodigy and removing the 5/3 threat.

annotations.description: Gem31P Hype passed priority during combat with Shambling Suit 5/3 attacking, taking 5 damage (going to 11 life) when they had Aether Spellbomb ready to bounce it. With Filigree Attendant 5/3 coming online next turn alongside Shambling Suit, the opponent threatens ~10 damage next turn, putting Gem31P in a very dangerous position. Bouncing the Suit would save 5 damage and force the opponent to re-spend 3 mana replaying it, buying a critical turn of tempo.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, taking 5 damage from Shambling Suit.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Aether Spellbomb (paying {U} from the untapped Island) to bounce Shambling Suit back to opponent's hand, preventing 5 damage and gaining tempo against a board that threatens lethal next turn.

annotations.description: Gem31P declined to attack with either creature when the opponent only had Locthwain Gargoyle 0/3 and Walking Ballista 1/1 as untapped blockers. Attacking with both 2/2s would force opponent to block with both - killing the Walking Ballista (removing a growing threat) and dealing 1 chip damage. With Filigree Attendant 5/3 and Shambling Suit 5/3 coming online next turn, Gem31P is falling behind and needs to press any advantage now.
annotations.actionTaken: Did not attack with any creatures.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Phyrexian Broodlings and Entomber Exarch. Opponent must block with Gargoyle and Ballista or take 4 damage. Either way, Gem31P trades favorably or deals significant damage. Could also Douse in Gloom the Walking Ballista pre-combat to ensure 2 damage gets through and gain 2 life.

annotations.description: Shambling Suit 5/3 is attacking and the player passed without using Aether Spellbomb to bounce it, taking 5 unnecessary damage. With Filigree Attendant 5/3 (flying) coming online next turn, the opponent will be threatening 10 damage per turn. At 16 life, this damage adds up fast and the tempo from bouncing the Suit would buy critical time.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority during combat, taking 5 damage from Shambling Suit.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Aether Spellbomb (pay {U}, sacrifice) targeting Shambling Suit to bounce it, preventing 5 combat damage and forcing the opponent to spend 3 mana replaying it, buying a crucial turn against the developing board.

annotations.description: Taking 12 damage (going to 4 life) when Aether Spellbomb could bounce one of the two 6-power attackers, saving 6 damage and leaving at 10 life instead. At 4 life, Gem31P is in immediate lethal range from Walking Ballista activations, any attacker, or burn. At 10 life, they have much more time to stabilize.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without using any abilities, taking 12 combat damage (16 → 4 life).
annotations.betterLine: Activate Aether Spellbomb paying {U} to bounce Filigree Attendant (6/3 flyer), reducing incoming damage to 6 and going to 10 life. Filigree Attendant is the best bounce target since it costs 4 mana to replay and its power scales with artifacts. Could also cast Douse in Gloom for the 2 life gain on top of the bounce.

annotations.description: Gem31P passed priority during combat instead of using Aether Spellbomb to bounce the unblocked Filigree Attendant 6/3, taking 6 unnecessary damage (16 → 10 life). The opponent has a very threatening board with Walking Ballista and will replay the Attendant, putting Gem31P in a precarious position at 10 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, taking 6 damage from unblocked Filigree Attendant
annotations.betterLine: Activate Aether Spellbomb (pay U, sacrifice) to return Filigree Attendant to opponent's hand, saving 6 life and forcing opponent to spend 4 mana to replay it. This buys a crucial turn of tempo while staying at a healthier 16 life.

annotations.description: Gem31P took 5 damage from a 5/3 flying Filigree Attendant while at 10 life, dropping to 5 life. They had Aether Spellbomb available to bounce the attacker (costing just {U}), which would save 5 life and buy a full turn since the opponent's lands are all tapped. At 5 life with a 5/3 flyer and Walking Ballista on the other side, the game is nearly unwinnable. At 10 life with the opponent needing to spend {2}{U}{U} to replay the Attendant, there's much more room to find answers.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, taking 5 damage from Filigree Attendant (10 → 5 life).
annotations.betterLine: Activate Aether Spellbomb ({U}, sacrifice) to bounce Filigree Attendant to opponent's hand, preventing 5 damage and staying at 10 life. The opponent's lands are all tapped so they can't replay it this turn, buying crucial tempo.

annotations.description: Cast Whirler Rogue while Phyrexian Rager's ETB draw trigger was still on the stack, committing all 4 available mana before seeing the drawn card. The draw could have revealed information that changes the optimal line (e.g., drawing a better instant-speed play or a card that changes combat math).
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Whirler Rogue in response to Phyrexian Rager's ETB trigger, before drawing the card.
annotations.betterLine: Let Phyrexian Rager's ETB trigger resolve first (draw a card, lose 1 life), see what was drawn, then cast Whirler Rogue in the precombat main phase. Information before commitment is a fundamental sequencing principle.

annotations.description: Attacked with only Filigree Attendant (6) and Drownyard Explorers (2) for 8 damage against opponent at 9 life, when Walking Ballista could have joined the attack for exactly 9 = lethal. All opponent creatures are summoning sick and all lands tapped, so nothing could interfere.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with Filigree Attendant and Drownyard Explorers for 8 damage total
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Filigree Attendant, Drownyard Explorers, and Walking Ballista for exactly 9 damage = lethal. While pinging with Ballista post-combat also works, attacking for clean lethal is simpler and avoids any risk of forgetting the ping.

annotations.description: With the opponent at 9 life and lethal on board through flyers (8 damage) plus ground creatures, there's no reason not to fire off Walking Ballista's ping for 1 damage now. The Ballista as a 1/1 attacker isn't better than a guaranteed ping since the opponent has ground blockers. Pinging now locks in damage and plays around potential interaction like Aether Spellbomb bouncing Filigree Attendant.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed on activating Walking Ballista's ping ability
annotations.betterLine: Activate Walking Ballista to deal 1 damage to opponent (going to 8 life), then attack with all flyers for 8 damage for exactly lethal, playing around potential bounce effects on the Attendant.

annotations.description: Gem31P Hype is at 9 life facing 13 points of incoming damage (Locthwain Gargoyle 2, Walking Ballista 1, Filigree Attendant 6, Drownyard Explorers 2, Runed Servitor 2). Without blocking, this is lethal. They had Phyrexian Rager and Whirler Rogue available as blockers and Aether Spellbomb to bounce the Filigree Attendant. By bouncing Filigree Attendant and blocking Drownyard Explorers and Runed Servitor, they would only take 3 damage (Gargoyle + Ballista) and survive at 6 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Declared no blockers, taking 13 lethal damage.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Aether Spellbomb to bounce Filigree Attendant (6/3), block Drownyard Explorers with Phyrexian Rager, block Runed Servitor with Whirler Rogue. Take only 3 damage, survive at 6 life.

annotations.description: Gem31P Hype is at 9 life facing 13 damage from attackers (2 from Gargoyle flying + 6 from Filigree Attendant flying + 1 Ballista + 2 Explorers + 2 Servitor). Even with optimal blocks on ground creatures, the 8 flying damage plus at least 1 ground damage is lethal. Aether Spellbomb can bounce Filigree Attendant (6 power flyer) for just {U}, reducing incoming damage to survivable levels.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Aether Spellbomb, accepting lethal damage.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Aether Spellbomb paying {U} to bounce Filigree Attendant, then block optimally to survive at ~5 life. This is the only way to survive this combat.
